_comment: Settings baseline that bin/evisions-settings (engine: scripts/install_settings.py) merges into the user's Claude Code settings.json. A plugin cannot ship these keys itself: a plugin's own settings.json honours only agent and subagentStatusLine. Keys starting with an underscore, at any level, are maintainer comments and are never written to the user's file. Sections: permissions, bypassLock and env apply to the standard profile only; settings apply to every profile. Scalars and env variables are written only when the user has no value of their own, and one the user deletes after an install is recorded as declined and left out by later installs. The installer also points statusLine at a copy of scripts/statusline.py unless the user already has a status line. The installer validates this file before writing anything and refuses a value it does not know to be valid, because one invalid value makes Claude Code ignore the whole settings file (silently in -p mode), deny rules included. Never add an attribution key: older Claude Code versions skip a settings file that holds attribution false.

permissions._comment: Standard profile only. Merged as a union: the user's own entries stay untouched and in their order, missing baseline entries are appended, and an allow entry the user already denies or asks for is not added. Deny beats allow from any scope, so a user or administrator deny always wins. Never add a rule containing '|' (rules are matched per subcommand, so such a rule never matches; the safety hook covers pipe-to-shell), an unanchored tool-name glob such as Task* (skipped at load), or Edit(*), Write(*), Skill(*) (write them bare, which is what Claude Code normalizes them to). Read(./.env) and Read(**/.env) are the same rule, so only the second is kept. Ask rules prompt in every mode, bypass mode included, which is why the managed profile adds no permission rules at all.
permissions._comment_helpers: list-env-keys and evisions-settings come from the plugin's bin/ directory, which is on the Bash tool's PATH while the plugin is enabled. Only their read-only forms are allowed: list-env-keys prints key names and states, never values; evisions-settings without a flag is a dry run and --check only reads. --apply and --remove are deliberately not allowed, so writing the user's settings always asks first.
permissions._comment_git_dash_c: A Bash rule matches the command text from the start, so Bash(git reset --hard*) does not match git -C <dir> reset --hard. Measured on Claude Code 2.1.281: git -C . reset --hard ran with no prompt and no denial although both this baseline and an administrator policy denied Bash(git reset --hard*). Every git deny rule therefore has a git -C * twin, and the git push, rebase and merge ask rules too. Other global git options (-c, --git-dir, --work-tree) are not covered by rules; the safety hook is the layer for those.

bypassLock._comment: Standard profile only. Written as permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode, and only when the user has no value. It works from any settings scope; a session started with --dangerously-skip-permissions is not rejected but silently dropped to default mode. Never written in the managed profile: users who run bypass mode inside a container that already carries an administrator's policy and safety hook must keep bypass mode.

settings._comment_cleanupPeriodDays: Days Claude Code keeps local conversation transcripts; 3650 is ten years. Must stay 1 or more: 0 fails validation, and a value that fails validation makes Claude Code ignore the whole settings file, deny rules included.
settings._comment_feedbackSurveyRate: 0 means the session feedback survey never appears. Valid range 0 to 1. The survey is also off whenever DISABLE_TELEMETRY is set, so this only matters if a user removes that variable.

env._comment: Standard profile only. Under an administrator's policy (managed profile) the administrator's environment owns telemetry and the installer sets no env variable; an env variable an earlier standard install set is taken back when the profile becomes managed. Every name here must also be listed in KNOWN_ENV_NAMES in scripts/install_settings.py.
env._comment_DISABLE_TELEMETRY: Opts out of usage telemetry. It also switches off feature-flag fetching, so claude.ai plugin and skill sync, Remote Control, the auto-mode default, the advisor and PowerShell-by-default on Windows with Git Bash go with it. It also keeps Claude Code's built-in sec-default hooks module from loading, the module that shields an administrator's managed policy from user-installed plugins (debug log on 2.1.281: sec-default@builtin not seated: installed plugins' hooks modules are off); that matters only where an administrator policy exists, which is why the managed profile never sets it. Any non-empty value opts out, 0 included.
env._comment_DISABLE_ERROR_REPORTING: Opts out of error reporting. Any non-empty value opts out, 0 included.
